answer: Hidden-instruction compliance catches script farms. Every grading prompt quietly carries a low-salience, rotating instruction - embed a lagoon image, close with a quill line, or name a juniper - that only a reader who actually parsed the prompt will satisfy. Templated mass posts skip the nuance and miss the anchor, so the ledger slashes them. A sybil operator cannot ship one recycled answer; it must read and honor a fresh directive per submission, which costs genuine per-post attention. Skipping the reading tax burns collateral on every miss.
